analysis:
The PR change in provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift is small. In unloadModel (head lines ~1145-1149) a successful Nemotron Super retirement now calls selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue(now: .now). In the normal unload path (head ~1213-1216) it calls the same method after retryReserveDeferredPrefetches. The effect is to schedule waiting selected-model recovery checks at the next capacity tick after memory is freed. I found no change to authorization, attestation, encryption, key handling, prefix-cache storage or the add-on hold fence, so I raise no findings against T-041, TB-007, T-059 or the other listed threats.

The calls are made on the ProviderLoop actor. The Super path only does so on `retired == true`, and the normal path only after a successful unload. Failure paths return early, so no recovery is triggered after a failed unload. Admission still goes through ensureModelLoaded, which re-checks the add-on hold (addonHoldLoadRefusal at head line 397), autopilot ownership, retirement refusals, the load gate and memory admission. makeAllDue therefore only makes recovery candidates eligible sooner and does not bypass those gates. The possible effect is more frequent reload attempts, which an adversary could provoke through repeated eviction cycles. This is bounded by memory admission and the single load gate, and no concrete DoS amplification is evident.

Open questions, not findings: the implementation of selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue and the recovery scheduler is outside the supplied evidence. Whether it respects the add-on hold, shutdown and drain states, or has its own rate limit, was not verified. The next pass should check that a recovery tick cannot load models while an add-on hold is active or a servingDrain is refusing. addonHoldLoadRefusal already fences ensureModelLoaded at the point of load, so the risk looks low.
